title: Meeting time calculation
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the time until the cars meet using their relative speed and initial separation.

title: Bird's total distance
description: Essential: Student uses the bird's constant speed and the meeting time to compute the total distance flown, yielding 400 m.

title: Bird's displacement
description: Important: Student correctly identifies that the bird's final displacement equals the displacement of Car A (or B) at the meeting time.

title: Average speed definition
description: Important: Student applies the definition of average speed (total distance / total time) to the bird's motion.

title: Final average speed
description: Essential: Student calculates the bird's average speed as 10 m/s, matching the ratio of its displacement to the total time.

title: Relative motion reasoning
description: Optional: Student uses a relative motion approach to simplify the problem, such as considering the closing speed of the cars.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Student maintains consistent units (meters, seconds, m/s) throughout the solution.

title: Infinite series misconception
description: Pitfall: Student attempts to sum an infinite geometric series for the bird's trips, which is unnecessarily complex and prone to error.

title: Average speed vs. velocity
description: Pitfall: Student confuses average speed with average velocity, incorrectly using displacement for the speed calculation.
